thread:
maria: FYI — Acme (acct: acme-inc) says their Feb invoice is ~6.3k tokens higher than the dashboard. They ran month-end reconciliation and flagged the delta.

raj: Ack. Do we have the invoice line item breakdown? might be a plan-change proration or overage.

maria: Invoice shows:
- plan base: 200k tokens
- overage: 37,512 tokens (billed)
Dashboard (All apps -> Acme -> Usage, Feb 1-28) shows total consumed tokens = 31,204.
They say no obvious spikes in their app logs.

emma: Thanks — two quick checks: 1) did they toggle caching or enable prefix KV caching in the middle of the month? dashboard excludes cached-satisfied requests from token meter, invoice should include raw model tokens. 2) timezone / cutoff mismatch?

maria: They said they enabled a server-side response cache on Feb 16th but still expect cached hits to reduce bill (their assumption). We need to confirm how our metering treats cache hits.

tom: Metering summary: billed tokens are computed at the model inference layer (post-decoding) before any HTTP-level caching. Dashboard uses aggregated job metrics which by default filter out 304 cache responses unless you check "include cached" toggle. There is a toggle.

maria: Hmm — they definitely rely on dashboard default view. Their ops said they never flipped "include cached" on.

raj: That could explain some delta but 6k tokens is significant. Can someone run an ad-hoc query across our ingest logs to compare billed_token_sum vs dashboard_token_sum for acct "acme-inc" Feb 1-28? If we get per-day breakdown we can see where the gap appears.

emma: Running quick SQL now against billing_aggregates dataset.

emma: ```sql
-- per-day billed vs dashboard-aggregated tokens
SELECT day, sum(billed_tokens) as billed, sum(dashboard_tokens) as dashboard
FROM billing_aggregates
WHERE account_id = 'acct_acme_inc' AND day BETWEEN '2025-02-01' AND '2025-02-28'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```

emma: Output snippet:
- 2025-02-01: billed 1,240  dashboard 1,240
- 2025-02-15: billed 4,800  dashboard 4,120  <-- gap emerges
- 2025-02-16: billed 12,400 dashboard 8,200  <-- huge gap day (cache enabled)
- rest of month: billed/dashboard aligned-ish

maria: That matches when they enabled their cache. If billed counts model tokens irrespective of cache hits, and dashboard default excludes cached responses, that explains it. But the customer insists they shouldn't be billed for cached responses — can we confirm our billing contract wording?

tom: Contract / pricing page wording: "Billing is based on model inference tokens generated by the service at the time of model execution. Responses served entirely from Redwood-managed cache may be excluded when explicitly configured to route through the caching layer with cache-hit suppression set on meter." In short: cached responses can be excluded, but only if customer uses Redwood-managed cache integration and sets the meter flag. Sounds like they used a self-hosted cache in front of our API. If their cache prevented requests from reaching our runtime, we wouldn't bill. But their logs show requests still reached us (we saw 200s from our edge).

maria: Customer-provided logs show many 200s to /v1/generate on Feb 16, and they thought those were cache hits (served from their proxy). We have edge logs that show our request_id and response_size. I can share an anonymized example.

maria: ```
# customer log (their proxy):
2025-02-16T09:12:05Z "GET /proxy/gen?id=abc123" 200 cache: HIT
# our edge log for same window:
2025-02-16T09:12:05.013Z request_id=01FJ... status=200 model=t5-xl tokens_in=12 tokens_out=188 billed_tokens=200
```

raj: So their proxy declared HIT but still forwarded the request to us (maybe for validation or telemetry). That would cause both the appearance of a cache hit in their layer and a billed inference on our side.

emma: I've drafted a short explanation and suggested next steps for the CS rep to share with Acme: 1) show per-day diff and sample paired logs showing the proxy HIT + forwarded request 2) explain billing policy re: meter flag / Redwood-managed cache 3) offer to run a one-time adjustment if customer provides evidence that requests were fully satisfied locally and never reached our runtime (edge request_id absent).

maria: Sounds good. Customer is asking for a credit for the 6,308 token delta. Can Finance review if we can offer a one-off credit (small amount) while we clarify long-term solution? @billing-bot can you attach invoice 2025-02-ACME and compute USD amount for 6,308 tokens at their plan rate (0.0006 USD/token)?

billing-bot: Attached invoice 2025-02-ACME.pdf. Computed amount for 6,308 tokens at 0.0006 USD/token = $3.78.

tom: If finance approves, we can issue a $3.78 credit. Also propose we add an explanatory note in dashboard UI when "include cached" is off to call out that third-party proxy caches that still forward requests will still incur billing.

maria: Customer accepted that workflow. They'll send us examples of proxy logs where they claim full local serve (no outbound). We'll validate against our edge logs, and finance will confirm the credit.

raj: Filed internal follow-up ticket INF-7893 to: 1) verify logging pairing heuristics, 2) add UI hint in dashboard, 3) update KB article on caching vs billing.

maria: Closing loop — thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
